newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 1.00 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 1.00 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open unchanged to 1.00 cent per lb lower Monday in line with losses overnight in London, dealers said.
LIFFE robusta futures were broadly lower by midday Monday after a firm start, pressured by origin sales. At the break, benchmark September was down $33 at $1,765 a tonne, traded $1,805 to $1,765.
The New York arabica market was closed on Friday in observance of U.S. Independence Day.

Thursday, benchmark September settled down 4.00 cents at 168.35 cents after trading from 167.50 to 174 cents. Spot July ended 8.50 cents lower, while the outer months closed down 1.00 to up 1.50 cents.
Technically, September faced near-term chart support at 167.00 and then 165.00 cents. Resistance was seen at 175.00 cents, traders said.
Weather Services Corp forecast on Monday mild to warm weather in Brazil's coffee belt, with no damaging cold weather expected for the next five days.
Following the close of business on Thursday, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 725 60-kg bags as of July 2, 50,550 bags. An additional 37,295 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

In other news, The International Coffee Organization (ICO) said on Monday producing members' exports reached 81.75 million 60-kg bags in the 12 months to May 1997, up sharply from 73.02 million in the same 1996 period.
In May, exports rose slightly to 7.03 million bags from 7.02 million in April. This compares with 6.60 million in May 1996.
